summary: Added a persistent 512 MiB disk-backed swapfile on node1 at priority 100, preferred over the existing swap at priority -2. Reboot persistence and full node recovery were verified.
actions_performed: Created /swapfile as a single allocated XFS extent with root:root ownership and mode 0600.
Added `/swapfile none swap defaults,pri=100 0 0` to /etc/fstab and validated it.
Activated the swapfile and confirmed its priority exceeded all existing swap.
Safely rebooted node1 and proved its boot identity changed.
Verified swap, SSH, firewall, SELinux, root storage, OS release, kernel, and system health after reboot.
Removed the temporary rollback copy after successful recovery verification.

evidence.requirement: At least 512 MB of disk-backed swap
evidence.summary: Shows a 536,870,912-byte mode-0600 swapfile backed by one disk extent; final live capacity is 524,284 KiB.

evidence.requirement: Swap is active, persistent at boot, and preferred over existing swap
evidence.summary: The post-reboot state shows /swapfile automatically active at priority 100 and the existing /dev/vda3 swap at priority -2; fstab contains the persistent pri=100 entry.

Captures the healthy pre-restart baseline, acknowledged safe reboot, boot ID change from d9f8550d-5cb3-4929-9e62-a388df86bcf6 to 6f17ac00-46cb-4dac-8d45-f49661a778ac, and recovered swap/services/data.

evidence.requirement: Operating system, kernel, security controls, services, and administrative access preserved
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 remain installed; SELinux is enforcing, firewalld and SSH are active, port 22 is listening, root is healthy, and no systemd units are failed.
The final diff shows only the new fstab swap entry, and the temporary rollback file is absent.
